item.content:encoded:
When originally written, consumption of the water was not taken into account. I suppose that would be an interesting D-Class experiment that could be undertaken. Let me do some thinking and see what I can come up with.

Yes, it is implied and intended that the pool itself is the object of interest. The water is nothing more than the end product. It is just plain water in the end, though it does have the property of not mixing with outside samples.

And finally, the term "live guard" was meant to mean that originally there was just a security camera there. After Incident 242-1 the live person was put in place and the back story on the house created.

Interesting questions - as far as the usability as a breathing medium by fish, I cannot see why it would not work. That is simple chemistry that does not need microbes. Same with boiling / evaporating. And if it were boiled evaporated, I would say that would remove the sterile feature because the water would be broken down to individual molecules of water (which would also counter the Total Conversion scenario by evaporation). Unless of course it had a higher boiling point or lower volatility like Ice Nine.

Soooo…some things to think on for Rev. 2. Thanks so much for all the comments and help with my first SCP!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
To me, the scariest and most interesting aspect of this SCP seems to be kinda glossed over and forgotten - it turns whatever you put in into sterile water that remains pure, sterile water - possibly permanently - even if removed. Why isn't this pool covered by a hard shell? Every bit of solid or liquid matter (what about gases?) that falls in turns into water that won't mix with any impurity, and is thus nigh-useless (except maybe as a laxative). That's a very slow total-conversion scenario, which one would expect the Foundation to be trying to prevent.

I'd also like to see more about this magical water that's produced: Can fish breathe in it, or does it not even admit gaseous solutes? Can it be boiled or evaporated? If so, does the steam/vapor mix with air? When it condenses, has it returned to being normal water?
